indicator_definition: The water exploitation index (WEI+) measures freshwater abstraction as a proportion of the available renewable freshwater resources (long-term average annual renewable freshwater resources minus environmental flow requirements). It is expressed as a percentage. Values above 20% indicate water stress; above 40% indicate severe water stress.
rationale: Water scarcity is an increasing threat to ecosystems, economies and human well-being. Monitoring freshwater abstraction relative to available resources is essential for sustainable water management. Progress means maintaining the water exploitation index below stress thresholds through efficient water use and resource management.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national water statistics reported by member states. Freshwater abstraction covers water withdrawn from rivers, lakes, reservoirs and groundwater for all uses. Available resources are estimated from long-term hydrological data adjusted for environmental flow requirements.
